newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian economy seen strong through 2000--Finmin.
newsitem.headline: Russian economy seen strong through 2000--Finmin.

text.p: Russia's financial performance will be strong through the end of the century, a Finance Ministry expert said on Monday.
Jochen Wermuth, head of the ministry's economic expert group told investors Russia deserved an improved sovereign credit rating.

He said Russia's performance had improved significantly in key areas used by agencies to determine a rating, including balance of payments, public debt, fiscal policy, inflation, and gross reserves as well as the general political situation.

"There's a very very serious view that, by the year 2000, inflation is about three, four, five percent, the deficit is about three, four, five percent (of GDP) and debt (domestic and foreign) to GDP is 50 percent," said Wermuth. "Russia qualifies for Maastricht criteria."

First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, who is also Finance Minister, said on Saturday that Russia, which last week launched a third, $2.0 billion Eurobond, would seek a new credit rating in the autumn.
